findings.title: Edits go unverified because no validation command runs after changes
findings.reason: In 40 analyzed sessions, 330 edit events were observed with zero subsequent validation commands. Population coverage shows 0 of 186 sessions contained any check. The diagnostic flag 'no-reviewed-relevant-check-evidence' is present. The project has available validation commands (pnpm typecheck, pnpm build) but they are never invoked after edits. The sole candidate with actual code changes (1 edit, 1 file) closed as 'changed-without-check'. Zero project-level Hooks exist to trigger validation automatically. This means changes may introduce undetected regressions and the user is the sole validation mechanism.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Rule owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add the smallest owned validation route for post-edit verification.

## What to do

Create a project-level Rule or AGENTS.md instruction that requires running `pnpm typecheck` after any source file edit. The project already has this command in package.json.

## Validation

- After making edits, run `pnpm typecheck` and confirm it exits 0
- If typecheck fails, fix the error before handing off to the user

findings.title: Agent lacks scoped project instructions for a 42-source-file codebase
findings.reason: The project profile shows agentInstructions.status='missing' with zero AGENTS.md files for a repository with 42 source files. The suggested minimum is 1. The project has complex business logic spanning eBay, Amazon, and Shopee integrations, Electron desktop framework, and Prisma backend, but no scoped instructions guide the agent on project structure, validation commands, safety boundaries, or coding conventions. Zero project-level Rules exist (all 3 Rules are global or plugin scope). The project has accumulated 111 project-level Memory entries including 12 common pitfalls and 12 code specifications, but these are not formalized as deterministic project-level instructions.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Document owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:

findings.title: Task completion cannot be confirmed at any acceptance boundary
findings.reason: Population coverage shows 0 of 186 sessions with structured completion signals and 0 with user correction signals. The only acceptance signal observed is 'assistant-handoff' in 16 of 186 sessions (8.6%). All 5 emitted candidates have acceptanceEvidenceCeiling='lead', meaning acceptance is inferred from agent behavior, not confirmed by user decision. In 287 task episodes, 0 were closed and 0 were recovered. This means the agent never formally confirms task completion and the user never provides correction signals, making delivery reliability unobservable.

findings.title: No documented rollback procedure exists for recovering from a bad change
findings.reason: The repository has a single-commit history ('Initial commit'), low history confidence, and no documented rollback or recovery procedure. While git itself provides reset and revert commands, the project has no runbook, script, or instruction that names the recovery owner, entrypoint, or postcondition. The project profile shows no recovery evidence, and 0 of 287 task episodes were recovered. In case of a bad change, the operator has no documented path to restore service.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Runbook owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Document the smallest owned recovery route for failed changes.

## What to do

Add a recovery section to AGENTS.md or a RUNBOOK.md that names: the recovery owner, the rollback command (git revert or git reset), the validation step after rollback (pnpm typecheck && pnpm build), and the postcondition (service restored to last known good state).

## Validation

- Confirm the recovery procedure is documented
- Verify the rollback command works by running git log --oneline -1

findings.title: Duplicate Memory title creates retrieval ambiguity
findings.reason: Asset integrity review found 1 exact title collision: two project-scope Memory entries share the same normalized title. The review covered all 112 Memory titles without truncation. The integrity finding is advisory and explicitly states the collision proves only title metadata naming collision, not body duplication or current impact. However, exact same-scope title collisions can cause retrieval to return conflicting entries, and the quality gates require an ordinary Low governance finding for exact collisions. A separate similarity candidate (80% title match) was found but remains deferred per quality gate policy on near matches.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Memory owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Resolve the exact Memory title collision.

## What to do

Use SearchMemory to locate the two entries with the same normalized title. Review their content to determine if they are duplicates or distinct entries with a naming conflict. If duplicates, update one to merge content and delete the other. If distinct, rename one to be unique.

## Validation

- Re-run the asset integrity review and confirm 0 exact collision groups
